title: The friends of Allah
hookLine: no fear on them nor grief: those who believe and are mindful (10:62–63)

lines: BLOCK B: PROPHETS, PARABLES AND LIGHT.
WHO ARE THE FRIENDS OF GOD?
cards: Block B: prophets, parables and light. Out of the long surahs revealed in Medina, and into a run of surahs usually placed in Mecca, named for prophets: Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim.

Surah ten carries Yunus's name, though he appears in it only once, near the end. Before that, the surah answers a question people in every age have asked about holy people. Who are the friends of God?
A few saints in a painting? A hermit on a mountain? Verse sixty-two gives a word for them, and verse sixty-three gives a definition that surprises people.

teach.h: NO FEAR ON THEM, NOR GRIEF.
teach.b: Pickthall's translation of verse sixty-two: "Lo! verily the friends of Allah are (those) on whom fear (cometh) not, nor do they grieve."
The word is awliya', friends, the plural of wali, from the same root you met in at-Tawbah, the one that means to be near. Last week it ran between believers. Here it runs between people and God.

teach.h: WHO? THOSE WHO BELIEVE AND ARE MINDFUL.
teach.b: Then the next verse defines them, in paraphrase: those who believe and keep mindful of God. That's all. Believe, and have taqwa.
No miracles required, no well-known name.
Over the centuries the word wali also came to mean a saint, especially in Sufi tradition, where great teachers are called awliya' and their tombs are visited.
Some Muslims honor those figures; others, especially in reformist movements, are wary of the practices around tombs. Both sides read the same verse, and both point to the same definition.
Now the promise: no fear, no grief.

teach.h: FEAR LOOKS AHEAD, GRIEF LOOKS BACK.
teach.b: Some commentators split the two this way: fear looks forward, at what might happen; grief looks back, at what already did. The friends of God are spared both, in the deepest sense.
And a hadith qudsi in Bukhari describes how someone draws near.
God says, in paraphrase: My servant comes close to Me through what I've made obligatory, and keeps coming closer through extra acts of devotion, until I love him.
And when I love him, I become the hearing he hears with, the sight he sees with. The friendship is not a rank you're born into. It's a nearness you walk into, one ordinary act at a time.

how: Muslims recite 10:62–64 as a comfort and as a description of God's friends; in many places the word wali is also used for revered saints whose tombs people visit, a practice some Muslims embrace and others discourage.

o: a friend, someone near; later also a saint
a hermit who lives apart on a mountain
a prophet sent to one particular people

games.q: the friends of God — tap the pairs.
p: those who believe and are mindful

s: the Qur'an says only well-known saints are friends of God
10:63 defines them as those who believe and keep mindful of God.
Yunus appears all through Surah Yunus
he's named only once, near the end; the surah still carries his name.
a hadith qudsi says God becomes the hearing of the one He loves
Bukhari: the servant draws near through obligations and extra devotion until God loves him.

games.q: someone asks you: who gets to be a friend of God? according to 10:63, what do you answer?
o: those who believe and are mindful of God.
games.why: those who believe and keep their duty to God. the verse gives a definition anyone can walk into.

practice: Notice where fear lives in you right now, the worry about something that hasn't happened, and name it quietly; then notice any grief, something from behind you.
Set the fear down in front of you and the grief behind you, and just sit in the middle, here. If you pray, you can recite the verse, or simply say: Ya Wali.

wordCard.voice: Wali. A friend, an ally, someone near; plural awliya'. The friends of God are those who believe and are mindful. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: friend, ally, protector; from w-l-y, to be near. plural awliya'.

carryVoice: Your line: no fear, no grief. Fear looks ahead; grief looks back. Day four hundred twenty-nine, done.

sources.q: Lo! verily the friends of Allah are (those) on whom fear (cometh) not, nor do they grieve.
